call_overview.title: About the call
call_overview.question: What does the call offer, and who can apply?

cards.title: What the call wants
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop, and which problem or need must it address?
cards.answer: Develop and demonstrate strategies to protect, restore and manage marine and coastal vegetated habitats, with local authorities and communities.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 136–139 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 136–139 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Project impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer: Improve the area and condition of marine habitats, sustain natural carbon storage and ecosystem resilience, and build local capacity to manage them.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 136–139 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Who it suits
cards.question: Who may lead, which partners must take part, and how must the work be shared?
cards.answer: This suits habitat-restoration organisations and research groups working with public authorities and local communities. Coordinate through one of at least three independent grant recipients from different eligible countries, including one in a European Union Member State. Combine restoration, monitoring, financing and community expertise.

cards.title: Innovation
cards.question: How new must the project be, and in what must it innovate?
cards.answer: Combine ecosystem restoration with new financing and incentive mechanisms, monitoring of multiple stressors, and practical ways for communities to participate.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 136–139 · Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?

cards.title: Demonstration and integration of work
cards.question: Where must the solution be demonstrated, and how must the work fit with existing systems?
cards.answer: Demonstrate restoration and protection at scale in the selected sea basin. Link habitat work to long-term management, ecological monitoring, financing, education and community involvement.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 136–139 · Scope

call_overview.title: Relevance to TenneT
call_overview.question: Why is this call relevant to TenneT?

cards.title: Why it matters to TenneT
cards.question: Why does this call matter to TenneT, and why can't TenneT take part itself?
cards.answer: Evidence on marine habitat recovery could inform TenneT’s offshore biodiversity planning and monitoring. The topic focuses on leading and managing habitat restoration and sets out no transmission-operator role.

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
The Commission indicates EUR 15.9 million for blue forest restoration. It expects 4 awards.
- Grant request: EUR 3.5–3.975 million per project is indicative. The Commission can select a different request.
- Funding form: Budget-based grant (paid using approved costs or rates for the funded work).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 136–139 · Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · p. 26 · Overview of this call
Large-scale demonstration of protection, restoration and management of blue forest ecosystems in European sea basins · Budget overview

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
For-profit organisations can receive up to 70% towards blue forest restoration.
- For-profit organisations: Up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow), leaving at least 30% to cover.
- Non-profit legal entities: Up to 100% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow).

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
Apply for blue forest restoration through the European Funding & Tenders Portal in one stage.
- Full proposal: 21 September 2027, 17:00 Brussels time. Submit Part A (online administration form) and Part B (technical proposal). Part B is limited to 40 pages.
- Opening: 9 February 2027.

cards.answer:
The grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules) sets the start date and duration for blue forest restoration.
- Required start: Work normally starts after the grant agreement is signed. A reasoned exception needs approval.

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Blue forest restoration proposals compete on research quality, impact and the quality of the delivery plan.
- Evaluation criteria: Excellence, impact, and quality and efficiency of implementation.
- Thresholds: At least 3/5 per criterion and 10/15 overall.
- Weighting: Impact is multiplied by 1.5 for the ranking.
- Ranking rules: Mission basin portfolio: The highest-ranked proposal in each basin receives priority if it clears all thresholds.

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
Blue forest proposals compete within their selected sea basin and may have to publish marine observations.
- Conditional — Satellite services: If the work uses satellite-based Earth observation, positioning, navigation or timing, beneficiaries (organisations formally responsible for funded work) must use Copernicus for Earth observation and/or Galileo or the European Geostationary Navigation Overlay Service for satellite positioning, navigation or timing.
- Conditional — Marine observations: If projects collect in-situ data and marine observations, beneficiaries must publish them through European Marine Observation and Data Network using principles that make data findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable.
